gaps: Division and regional land leaders: no divisional VP / Director of Land Acquisition, Land Development or Entitlements for Dream Finders is named in any public source opened. Job postings show the structure without names: a divisional VP of Land reports to the Division President and works with a Regional VP of Land and the National VP of Land (career.com posting, Chantilly VA, 2026-09). Only Regional VP of Land Operations Matt Childers (Texas and West) is named.

Regional presidents: only Liesel Cooper (Colorado plus Carolinas/Nashville scope announced 2024) is named. No regional president is published for Florida, Mid-Atlantic/Carolinas or Texas. The segment heads for Southeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest are not disclosed; COO Clint Szubinski (June 2026) runs operations.

No division leader found for: Southeast Florida, Southwest Florida, Savannah GA, Hilton Head / Bluffton SC, Charleston SC, Greenville SC, Myrtle Beach SC, Nashville TN, Raleigh NC, Wilmington NC, Southern Coast NC, Triad NC, Goldsboro NC, Charlotte NC (HBA board affiliation only: Jeff Ott), Auburn AL, Northern Colorado, Atlanta GA (post-acquisition leader not named), the DF Luxury Homes custom division (Jacksonville), and Craft Homes (Orlando).

Beazer Homes (DFH subsidiary since 2026-10-20): no post-closing division roster has been published, and Beazer's own releases and site name no division or area presidents. Only directory leads (theorg.com, unverified) were found: Las Vegas, Houston and Atlanta division presidents and two land executives. Nothing found for Beazer Phoenix, Southern California / Riverside, Sacramento, San Diego, Dallas, San Antonio, Indianapolis, Maryland / Delaware, Northern Virginia, Nashville, Orlando, Raleigh, Charleston or Myrtle Beach.

Former acquired-company leaders not carried as current: Ted Terry (Crescent Homes founder/CEO, named in the Feb 2024 acquisition release; no later source), Brian Hurley (Green River Builders founder/CEO, May 2025 release reads as a hand-off), Jack Rostetter (named President of a Carolinas division after the 2020 H&H acquisition; Leslie Groves now leads Fayetteville) and Henri Rodier (listed as Coventry CEO on theorg.com, undated).

For the corporate file, directory leads at Beazer (theorg.com, unverified): Erica Champion, Chief Investment Officer; Jim Moore, SVP of Operations; Henry Sprague, Corporate Land Acquisition Manager (profile updated 2026-01); Josh Turner, Land Development Manager (2026-07).
Division leaders in the remaining markets above (Florida, Carolinas, Nashville, Atlanta, Texas, Beazer markets): not searched by name, so these markets are unsearched rather than confirmed vacant.
